meaning: Short for Desi Hip Hop: rap and hip hop made by South Asian artists, especially in India. Fans use it for the whole scene, from underground cyphers to chart hits.
example: Been deep in DHH since Bayaan dropped.

meaning: From 'desh' (country). Means South Asian, or something from back home. A badge of pride in the scene rather than a label.
example: Desi flows, global sound.

meaning: The community of artists, producers and fans in a city or across the country. Every city now has its own scene with its own sound.
example: The Nagpur scene is on fire right now.

meaning: Hindi for a narrow lane or street. Stands for the working-class neighbourhoods where Mumbai rap began, and for staying true to where you come from.
example: From the gully to the main stage.

meaning: Bambaiya (Mumbai street slang) for a buddy or homie. Emiway Bantai made it part of his name and his label.
example: Kya bolta bantai?

meaning: The street dialect of Mumbai, a quick mix of Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati and English. It is the native tongue of gully rap.
example: Half the punchlines only hit if you speak Bambaiya.

meaning: 'Our time will come.' The hook from Gully Boy, co-written by DIVINE, that became the slogan for every underdog in the scene.
example: Still grinding. Apna time aayega.

meaning: 'We'll cause a storm.' From 'machana', to create chaos. Means you are about to take over, and Emiway turned it into a whole series.
example: New tape Friday, machayenge.

meaning: Hindi slang for drama, a fight or a mess. A 'kaleshi' person always starts trouble, which Raga turned into a viral hit.
example: Comment section mein full kalesh.

meaning: Chaos or uproar. Used as praise too: a bawaal verse is an amazing one.
example: That second verse was straight bawaal.

meaning: Literally 'strong', like kadak chai. Means hard, sharp or excellent.
example: Beat ekdum kadak hai.

meaning: A Mumbai street hustler with swagger and a loose tongue. The tapori character and his slang run all through Mumbai rap.
example: Tapori energy, tailored fit.

meaning: A bar is one line of a verse, usually one measure of the beat. Saying someone 'has bars' means their writing is sharp and quotable.
example: Only bars on this one, no hook.

meaning: The rhythm and cadence of how a rapper delivers words over the beat. Flow switches in the middle of a verse are a big part of DHH bragging rights.
example: Three different flows in one verse.

meaning: Multisyllabic rhymes, where several syllables rhyme in a row instead of just the last one. Hindi and Punjabi make these especially tricky, and fans count them.
example: KR$NA stacking multis like it's nothing.

meaning: A line built to land hard at the end of a thought, usually with a twist, a double meaning or a joke.
example: Rewound it three times for that punchline.

meaning: Puns, double meanings and switching between languages to make one line mean two things. Code-switching between Hindi and English makes DHH wordplay unique.
example: The wordplay on that hook is disgusting.

meaning: The repeated, catchy part of a song, sung or rapped. A strong hook turns a good verse into a hit.
example: Hook's stuck in my head for a week.

meaning: A rapper's section of a song, usually 12 to 16 bars. On a feature, everyone gets a verse and fans rank them.
example: Who had the best verse on Hola Amigo?

meaning: Rapping made up on the spot, or a verse over a beat with no song structure. Freestyles on YouTube and at cyphers launched many careers.
example: Dropped a freestyle before the album to warm up.

meaning: A circle of rappers taking turns on the same beat, live or on record. The backbone of the early Indian underground.
example: Met the whole crew at a Sunday cypher.

meaning: A song made to attack another artist. The 2020 Raftaar and Emiway exchange is one of the most famous diss chapters in DHH.
example: He replied with a diss in 48 hours.

meaning: A public feud between artists, usually played out through diss tracks and social media.
example: Everyone picked a side in that beef.

meaning: Short for featuring: a guest artist on someone else's track. Features are how scenes connect, and this archive maps them.
example: Siyaahi on the feat. was the best part.

meaning: Short for 'produced by', the credit for whoever made the beat. Fans follow producers as closely as rappers now.
example: Prod. Sez on the Beat? Instant play.

meaning: A beat made in the style of a known artist and sold or shared online, for example a 'Seedhe Maut type beat'. Where a lot of producers start.
example: Bought a type beat, wrote a whole EP on it.

meaning: A mixtape: a looser, often free or independent project. Many DHH classics are tapes rather than official albums.
example: Lunch Break is a tape, not an album.

meaning: A new release, or the moment it comes out.
example: Midnight drop, stay up.

meaning: Someone who was there early and earned respect. MTV Hustle 4 even gave Siyaahi the title OG Hustler.
example: Show some love to the OGs.

meaning: Independent artists outside the label and film machine. In DHH, coming from the underground is a point of pride.
example: Still underground, still selling out shows.

meaning: A diss aimed at artists accused of trading their sound for money, film songs or brand deals. The most common argument in any DHH comment section.
example: One Bollywood song and they're calling him a sellout.

meaning: The crowd space where fans jump and crash into each other at shows. Naam Sujal named a whole song after it.
example: Front row, straight into the moshpit.

meaning: The grind of making it with no shortcuts. Also MTV Hustle, the rap reality show that introduced many artists in this archive.
example: Day job by day, hustle by night.

meaning: Rap in regional languages like Malayalam, Tamil, Gujarati, Marathi, Haryanvi or Kashmiri. The fastest growing part of DHH.
example: Best verse of the year was in Gujarati.
